name: Elnathan
overview: Elnathan was a male Levite mentioned in the book of Ezra as the second Levite sent to Iddo. His role is noted specifically in Ezra 8:16, highlighting his participation in the return from exile. There are no additional personal details or notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Elnathan means 'G-d is given,' reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew name. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a clear acknowledgment of divine provision or gift.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Elnathan as a descendant of Levi, confirming his tribal affiliation and priestly lineage. Beyond this, no further family relationships are recorded for him in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Elnathan's significance lies in his role as a Levite who was part of the faithful group sent by Ezra to Iddo, which underscores the importance of Levites in the restoration and religious reforms after the exile. His mention in Ezra 8:16 situates him within the broader narrative of the return to Jerusalem and the reestablishment of proper worship. Though details are sparse, his inclusion highlights the continuity of Levitical service in God's redemptive plan for Israel.
